headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell-capable orchestration can leak data and cascade errors; Whisper is isolated but Kestra’s defaults are broad.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and run shell/subprocesses, so if Whisper outputs are manually copied or written into shared files, prompt-like content could influence downstream workflows. Whisper itself has no file write or network surface, so the pathway is one-way and requires an operator bridge, not a default direct channel.
conditions: IF the operator copies Whisper transcripts into Kestra-readable files
IF Kestra workflows parse those files as instructions or task definitions
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs in a separate directory from Kestra inputs
Require a human review step before any file from Whisper is used by Kestra
Use strict file-format validation for any imported text
Disable automatic ingestion of arbitrary text into workflow definitions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and messages, and it has broad network egress. Whisper has no network egress and no filesystem write, so the main leakage risk is Kestra exposing sensitive workflow data through its own outputs or external calls; the pair can move sensitive data into a broader processing surface in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows process sensitive inputs or artifacts
IF Kestra sends those materials to external services or logs them
mitigations: Restrict Kestra workflows from handling sensitive datasets
Turn off or minimize verbose logging for sensitive jobs
Route sensitive jobs only to approved internal endpoints
Redact secrets before workflow handoff
Separate Whisper processing from any sensitive Kestra workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad API access; Whisper is CLI-oriented but has no write or network capability. There is no direct write-write conflict from Whisper, but if both are run in the same workspace, Kestra can overwrite or consume Whisper artifacts, creating mutable-resource contention in default shared-directory deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory
IF Kestra workflows modify files that Whisper is reading or producing
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Use per-run unique filenames
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Mount Whisper inputs read-only where possible
Avoid placing both agents in the same git checkout

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra is an automation/orchestration agent that can act on workflow outputs, while Whisper produces speech transcripts that may be treated as authoritative text. If Kestra consumes Whisper output without verification, transcription errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions; Whisper has no built-in verification channel, so the pair needs an explicit review gate.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Whisper transcripts as inputs to automated tasks
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks transcript accuracy
mitigations: Insert a transcript review step before automation
Require confidence thresholds for downstream actions
Log source audio alongside transcripts for audit
Block irreversible actions until a human approves
Use structured extraction checks on Whisper output

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: Kestra handles logs, messages, and cloud data, while Whisper is audio/speech-only. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly evidenced and Whisper has no listed sensitive-data handling, this remains a low, documentation-limited risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra workflows
IF retention or residency policies differ between the systems
mitigations: Document data classes allowed in Kestra jobs
Set retention limits for logs and artifacts
Keep regulated audio out of shared workflows
Review vendor residency and DPA terms before deployment
